units.note: Name form 'Lagon' renders Λάγιον (Lagius); same person, spelling only, not changed here.

findings.quote: so that the enemy could not cross and fight from the embankments
findings.problem: ὅπως μὴ διαβαίνοντες οἱ πολέμιοι προσμάχωνται τοῖς χώμασιν: so that the enemy could not wade across and attack the moles/embankments (the Roman works). The English reverses the direction of the action.
findings.proposed_fix: so that the enemy could not cross and attack the embankments

findings.quote: an overbearing man must never say or do anything proud
findings.problem: δεῖ μηδέποτε λέγειν μηδὲ πράττειν μηδὲν ὑπερήφανον ἄνθρωπον ὄντα: one must never, being human (mortal), say or do anything arrogant. ἄνθρωπον ὄντα is 'being a man', not 'an overbearing man'; the English garbles the moral.
findings.proposed_fix: one who is only human must never say or do anything arrogant

findings.quote: because not only she herself but also the children were being saved from his fate
findings.problem: διότι τὸ μὲν ἐκείνου μέρος οὐκ αὐτὴ μόνον, ἀλλὰ καὶ τὰ τέκνα σῴζεται: because, so far as it lay with him (the general), not only she but the children were saved. τὸ ἐκείνου μέρος is 'as far as he was concerned', not 'from his fate'.
findings.proposed_fix: because, as far as it rested with him, not only she herself but also the children were being saved

findings.quote: after saying that she herself would obtain no private salvation from the general by deserting, he could
findings.problem: πῶς αὐτῇ μὲν φάσκων οὐδὲν κατ᾽ ἰδίαν παρὰ τοῦ στρατηγοῦ πορίζοιτο τὴν σωτηρίαν αὐτομολήσας: how, saying nothing to her (αὐτῇ οὐδὲν φάσκων), he had deserted and privately procured his own safety from the general. The subject of πορίζοιτο is Hasdrubal; the negation belongs to 'saying nothing to her', not to her obtaining safety. Sense inverted.
findings.proposed_fix: without saying a word to her, he had deserted and privately secured his own safety from the general, and how he could

findings.quote: he dared now to sit here crowned, while he had many times said that the day would never come when he would see Hasdrubal alive
findings.problem: πῶς δὲ παρὰ τούτοις τολμᾷ καθῆσθαι νῦν θαλλοὺς ἔχων πρὸς οὓς... πολλάκις οὐδέποτε ταύτην ἔσεσθαι τὴν ἡμέραν, ἐν ᾗ συμβήσεται τὸν ἥλιον ἅμα καθορᾶν Ἀσδρούβαν ζῶντα: he sits beside these men (παρὰ τούτοις) holding suppliant branches (θαλλούς), men to whom (πρὸς οὓς) he had often [gap; verb of saying lost] that the day would never come when the sun (τὸν ἥλιον) would see Hasdrubal alive and his country burning. English smooths the lacuna after πρὸς οὓς, drops 'to these men', and makes 'he' rather than the sun the seer.
findings.proposed_fix: he dared now to sit beside these men holding suppliant branches, men to whom he had [...] many times that the day would never come when the sun would see Hasdrubal alive

units.note: Final paragraph is an explicitly marked editorial summary of the papyrus-like broken text; left as is.

findings.quote: [...] The text here is badly broken in the witness, but the sense is that Polybius is completing Scipio’s remark about the danger of overconfidence and the importance of good judgment.
findings.problem: Only the opening lines are broken. The Greek then has a fully legible passage that the English omits: καὶ τοῦτ᾽ εἴρηται παρὰ τῷ ποιητῇ· καὶ ἐπιστρέψας ἐξ αὐτῆς καὶ λαβόμενός μου τῆς δεξιᾶς 'ὦ Πολύβιε,' ἔφη 'καλὸν μέν, ἀλλ᾽ οὐκ οἶδ᾽ ὅπως ἐγὼ δέδια καὶ προορῶμαι μή ποτέ τις ἄλλος τοῦτο τὸ παράγγελμα δώσει περὶ τῆς ἡμετέρας πατρίδος.' ταύτης δὲ [gap]. The summary also misattributes: it is Scipio who speaks, to Polybius. Intact text treated as lacuna; the real gap after ταύτης δὲ is not marked.
findings.proposed_fix: [...] The opening lines are badly broken in the witness; Polybius is speaking, and a saying of the poet is cited. [...] And at once he turned and grasped my right hand and said, “Polybius, it is a fine thing; but somehow I fear and foresee that someday someone else will give this same order about our own country.” Of this [...]

units.note: After ταύτης δὲ the Greek breaks; the following sentence (δύναμιν πραγματικωτέραν καὶ νουνεχεστέραν) may not connect directly. Its current English ('lesson') is left untouched as outside the error classes.
Opening lacuna (πόλιν ὁρῶν...) is marked [...] in the English.
